prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment. Findings and their definitions: - Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion). - Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent. - Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis. - Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count. - Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space. - Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count. How to work: 1. Read the patient's image systematically first. 2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it. 3. Take the clinical indication into account. 4. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value. Clinical indication: chest pain and XXXX. Similar cases (most similar first): Case CXR2687 (similarity 0.977): FINDINGS: The heart size and mediastinal contours appear within normal limits. No focal airspace consolidation, pleural effusions or pneumothorax. Surgical clips overlying the left breast soft tissues. Multilevel degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. No acute bony abnormalities. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary findings. Case CXR2377 (similarity 0.969): FINDINGS: The heart size and pulmonary vascularity appear within normal limits. The lungs are free of focal airspace disease. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen. IMPRESSION: No evidence of active disease. Case CXR354 (similarity 0.967): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size. The mediastinum is stable. The lungs are clear. IMPRESSION: No acute disease. Case CXR2192 (similarity 0.966): FINDINGS: No focal lung consolidation. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.Heart size and pulmonary vascularity are within normal limits.Minimal degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. The previously
described XXXX deformity in the midthoracic spine is again seen. There is subcutaneous shunt catheter tubing along the anterior chest wall IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process. Case CXR2773 (similarity 0.965): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size and contour. The lungs are clear, without evidence of infiltrate. There is no pneumothorax or effusion. Mild degenerative changes at the lower thoracic spine. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease. Case CXR2237 (similarity 0.965): IMPRESSION: Heart size is normal. Lungs are clear. Stable 5 mm calcified left midlung granuloma. Calcified aortic XXXX. Case CXR1724 (similarity 0.964): FINDINGS: The lungs are mildly hyperinflated, with upper lobe areas of lung lucency suggesting obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema. No superimposed focal airspace consolidation is seen. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size is normal. IMPRESSION: Emphysema. Case CXR49 (similarity 0.964): FINDINGS: The heart, pulmonary XXXX and mediastinum are within normal limits. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. There is no focal air space opacity to suggest a pneumonia. There are degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. There is a calcified granuloma identified in the right suprahilar region. The aorta is mildly tortuous and ectatic. There is asymmetric right apical smooth pleural thickening. There are severe degenerative changes of the XXXX. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease. Case CXR2992 (similarity 0.963): FINDINGS: The lungs are clear. Heart size is normal. No pneumothorax. Calcified granuloma within the right lung base. IMPRESSION: Clear lungs. No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. . Case CXR301 (similarity 0.963): FINDINGS: Normal cardiomediastinal contours. Clear lungs bilaterally. No pneumothorax or large effusion. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
